statement.text:
a) Let t be an involution of a finite group G and suppose that the set D =
tG ∪{tx ty | x, y ∈ G, |tx ty | = 2} does not intersect O2 (G). Prove that if t ∈ O2 (C(d))
for any involution d from CD (t), then D = tG (and in this case the structure of the
group ⟨D⟩ is known).
    b) A significantly more general question. Let t be an involution of a finite group G
and suppose that t ∈ Z ∗ (N (X)) for every non-trivial subgroup X of odd order which
is normalized, but not centralized, by t. What is the group tG ?           A. A. Makhnëv
